body:
Friday Coding Kickoff

Today is Friday, March 27, 2026. Let's look at the actual code patterns that make Spring Boot feel like magic.

1. Creating a REST Endpoint

The bread and butter of Spring Boot. Use @RestController to tell Spring this class handles HTTP requests, and @GetMapping to map a specific URL path to a method.

2. Path Variables

Used to capture dynamic values directly from the URL path. This is standard for fetching specific resources, like an item ID in a retail POS system.

3. Request Parameters

Captured from the query string (the part after the ? in a URL). Useful for filtering, sorting, or searching through product lists.

4. Handling POST Data

When sending data to the server (like a new user or order), use @PostMapping and @RequestBody. Spring automatically converts the incoming JSON into a Java object.

5. Constructor Injection

The modern, recommended way to perform Dependency Injection. It makes your code easier to test and ensures required dependencies aren't null.

6. Reading Properties

Use the @Value annotation to pull specific configuration values from your application.properties or application.yml file.

7. Defining a Service Layer

Keep your controllers 'thin' by putting business logic in @Service classes. This keeps your code clean, modular, and reusable.

8. Creating a Data Repository

With Spring Data JPA, you don't write SQL. Just extend JpaRepository and Spring provides all the CRUD operations (save, delete, find) for you.

9. Global Exception Handling

Instead of messy try-catch blocks in every method, use @RestControllerAdvice to catch specific exceptions globally and return a clean error message.

10. Running Code on Startup

The CommandLineRunner interface is perfect for running logic (like seeding a database or logging system status) immediately after the app starts.
